rows.citation: Jatana, N., Suri, B., Kumar, P., et al. (2016). Test Suite Reduction by Mutation Testing Mapped to Set Cover Problem. Proceedings of the Second International Conference on Information and Communication Technology for Competitive Strategies, 1-6.
rows.model_type: general software programs (Triangle, Quadratic, TCAS subject programs); not a scientific or neuron model
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - program mutants define which test cases are needed; reduction preserves mutant-kill coverage (per abstract).
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - test cases are program inputs, loosely analogous to protocols; no electrical stimulation.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - test-suite reduction cast as set cover and solved greedily, a direct precedent for greedy protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract reports only a preliminary evaluation on three programs; full text not accessed, no held-out split described.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Greedy mutant-coverage set cover is established precedent and cannot be claimed. NeuroSem would apply it to stimulation protocols on NeuroML neuron models, with refinement-calibrated feature tolerances, admissible-mutant classification, and held-out models, a held-out mutation family, and cost-matched random baselines.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, authors, container, 2016-03-04, pages 1-6); OpenAlex work W2514273129 abstract. DBLP API returned a bot-check page (blocked); ACM full text not accessed.
rows.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (test suite minimization greedy set cover mutation); verified via Crossref works API

rows.citation: Liu, Y., Maini, P. K., & Baker, R. E. (2026). Optimal experiment design for practical parameter identifiability and model discrimination. Mathematical Biosciences, 399, 109710.
rows.model_type: ODE models of population growth (logistic, Richards) plus a linear signalling-pathway model in an appendix; not neuronal
rows.controlled_mutations: no - discriminates competing model structures or parameter sets, not single-fault edits.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - designs a time-varying external control input and compares continuous against bang-bang controls; no fixed protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - population and signalling outputs only.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - optimal control via Pontryagin's Maximum Principle to maximise model discrimination, and profile-likelihood identifiability for design.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - demonstrated on chosen synthetic model examples; no held-out models or splits seen in arXiv HTML.
rows.software: MATLAB analysis code, stated location https://github.com/liuyue002/experiment_design (page returned HTTP 200; contents not inspected)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Adjacent optimal-experiment-design precedent for choosing stimuli that separate models. NeuroSem instead selects a discrete, interpretable battery of standard current-clamp protocols by coverage of edit-induced mutants in NeuroML neuron models, with calibrated tolerances and held-out evaluation, rather than continuous optimal control between known candidate models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (authors, Mathematical Biosciences vol 399, article 109710, issued 2026-09); Semantic Scholar API abstract (arXiv 2506.11311, PubMed 42176891); arXiv HTML v1 full text (sections, discussion, code statement).
rows.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (optimal stimulus protocol design neuron model parameter identifiability); verified via Crossref works API | WebSearch hERG model discrimination query; arXiv abstract page metadata

rows.citation: Open Brain Institute (2026). eFEL: electrophysiology feature extraction library (efel 5.7.34). PyPI / GitHub. Associated paper: Mandge, D., Tuncel, A., Jaquier, A., et al. (2026). eFEL: electrophysiology feature extraction library. Bioinformatics, 42(6). doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btag328.
rows.model_type: feature-extraction library for neuronal voltage time series (in vitro and in silico); not a model
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - accepts many traces with stimulus start/end windows but does not define or run stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - extracts standard features (e.g. AP amplitude, AP width, baseline voltage) with a C++ core and Python wrapper.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - not applicable to a feature library.
rows.software: eFEL https://github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL ; PyPI efel 5.7.34 (uploaded 2026-08-25), LGPLv3 per PyPI classifier; LICENSE.txt says examples and tests are BSD-licensed
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Component NeuroSem plans to reuse, pinned to a recorded version; no novelty is possible for feature extraction. NeuroSem would add protocol execution, refinement-calibrated tolerances, mutant generation and classification, protocol selection, and held-out evaluation on top of it.
rows.verification_method: PyPI JSON API (version, license, homepage, author, requires_python >=3.10); raw GitHub README.md and LICENSE.txt (GitHub REST API rate-limited, 403); Crossref works API for 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag328 (8 authors, Bioinformatics 42(6), 2026). README lists Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19604220, but the Zenodo API returned 504 twice, so that DOI is unverified.
rows.found_via: PyPI JSON API https://pypi.org/pypi/efel/json (license LGPLv3; homepage github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL); earlier Zenodo versions surfaced in OpenAlex search (e.g. 10.5281/zenodo.30074 'eFEL 2.6')

rows.citation: Hines, M. L., Morse, T., Migliore, M., et al. (2004). ModelDB: A Database to Support Computational Neuroscience. Journal of Computational Neuroscience, 17(1), 7-11.
rows.model_type: web database of published computational neuroscience models across simulators
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - abstract describes entering, retrieving and running published models, not stimulation batteries.
rows.software: ModelDB web database (URL not retrieved in this session)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Infrastructure: a possible provenance source for fixture models, not a testing method. NeuroSem does behavioural drift detection, which ModelDB does not address according to its abstract.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (5 authors, JCNS 17(1):7-11, 2004-07); Europe PMC REST abstract (PMID 15218350, PMC3732827). PMC full-text XML via Europe PMC and NCBI efetch returned no body text, so only the abstract was read.

rows.citation: Miłkowski, M., Hensel, W. M., & Hohol, M. (2018). Replicability or reproducibility? On the replication crisis in computational neuroscience and sharing only relevant detail. Journal of Computational Neuroscience, 45(3), 163-172.
rows.model_type: conceptual / methodological analysis of computational neuroscience models in general
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Offers definitions: replication reruns original code, reproduction rebuilds a model without it. NeuroSem is an empirical testing method that gives finite evidence (not proof) of preserved tested behaviour after edits or translation; this paper supplies framing only.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (authors, JCNS 45(3):163-172, 2018-10-31); OpenAlex abstract; Springer open-access PDF keyword scan (LEMS/NeuroML named only as examples of description languages).
rows.found_via: OpenAlex search; Europe PMC citations of NeuroML 2010 and LEMS 2014

rows.citation: Metzner, C., Mäki-Marttunen, T., Zurowski, B., et al. (2018). Modules for Automated Validation and Comparison of Models of Neurophysiological and Neurocognitive Biomarkers of Psychiatric Disorders: ASSRUnit—A Case Study. Computational Psychiatry, 2, 74.
rows.model_type: neural network models of auditory steady-state response deficits: Beeman auditory-cortex model in GENESIS and NeuroML2, plus a Python theta-neuron network
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - each model runs in a control and a disorder-like parameter configuration; deliberate changes, but not single-fault mutation operators.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - five tests cover observations at several drive frequencies (20, 30, 40 Hz), plus a 10 Hz prediction test.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - spectral power at drive and harmonic frequencies of a simulated EEG/MEG-like signal; not single-cell eFEL-type features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - tests are fixed by the literature observations.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - models are scored against experimental observations; no held-out models or splits.
rows.software: ASSRUnit https://github.com/ChristophMetzner/ASSRUnit (SciUnit-based; README lists GENESIS, pyNeuroML and NEURON as optional dependencies)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: SciUnit-style validation of models against experimental data across several stimulus conditions. NeuroSem instead compares a model against its own edited versions under current-clamp protocols, with calibrated tolerances, controlled mutants, coverage-based protocol selection, and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (4 authors, Computational Psychiatry vol 2, page 74, issued 2018-07-01); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar abstract; arXiv 1712.06353 PDF full-text scan (models, tests, GitHub link); raw GitHub README. arXiv export API returned an empty response.
rows.found_via: Semantic Scholar API forward citations of SciUnit ICSE 2014, LEMS 2014 and F1000 unit-testing paper; Crossref-verified (abstract not retrieved)
